task.situation: The youth website ‘Mirror Talk’ is running a blog series called ‘What makes me … me?’, in which young people write about what shapes who they are. You have decided to write a blog post for the series.
task.instruction: In your blog post you should:
points: describe what shapes young people’s identity (e.g. music, style, languages, friends, family)
compare how young people express who they are online and offline
give advice to readers who feel under pressure to fit in

words.short: Give your blog post a title. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Give your blog post a title. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Blogbeitrag für eine Jugend-Website: Titel, Username, Datum und Uhrzeit, Einstieg mit Hook, klare Absätze, Schluss mit Aufruf zum Kommentieren. Drei Inhaltspunkte: was Identität prägt, online und offline vergleichen, Tipps gegen Anpassungsdruck. Den Titel wählen wir ganz zum Schluss.

focus.label: linking words in a chatty voice
focus.note: Marked: linking words that carry the blogger’s personal line of thought: reasons, examples, contrasts and afterthoughts in a chatty voice (because, since, for example, though, what’s more, that’s why, all in all …). ‘So’ at the start of a question or a call to the reader is not marked.

gaps.q: Who is the blogger’s best friend? First name only.
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vornamen für die beste Freundin oder den besten Freund. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: Which personal angle does our blogger take?
steps.de: Wählt den persönlichen Aufhänger, der sich durch Einleitung, Body paragraph 1 und Schluss zieht.

options.label: The playlist test
options.teaser: Our blogger believes a playlist says more about a person than a passport.

options.label: Dialect, German, English
options.teaser: Our blogger speaks Viennese dialect, standard German and English, sometimes all on the same day.

steps.q: How do we hook our readers?
steps.de: Der Einstieg führt zur großen Frage des Blogbeitrags. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction with a detail about our blogger that leads to the big question.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit einem Detail über unsere Bloggerin oder unseren Blogger fertigschreiben, das zur großen Frage führt.

options.label: Ask the readers a question
options.why: A direct question pulls readers in, and the funny detail makes them want to read on.

map.music: {{Want to know who I really am? Forget my passport}} and just press shuffle on my playlist. Within three songs, you’ll hear old-school hip-hop, a film soundtrack and something my dad simply calls ‘noise’. {{That got me thinking: what actually makes us}} who we are?
map.languages: {{How many different people can you be in one day?}} I’m at least three: I chat in Viennese dialect with my grandpa, speak standard German in class and switch to English for online gaming. {{That got me thinking: which version is the real me,}} and what makes us who we are?

map.music: {{Want to know who I really am? Forget my passport}} and just press shuffle on my playlist. Within three songs, you’ll hear old-school hip-hop, a film soundtrack and something my dad simply calls ‘noise’. My friends say they can guess my mood from the first track. {{That got me thinking: what actually makes us}} who we are, and how much of it do we choose ourselves?
map.languages: {{How many different people can you be in one day?}} I’m at least three: I chat in Viennese dialect with my grandpa, speak standard German in class and switch to English for online gaming. In each language, I tell different jokes and even laugh differently. {{That got me thinking: which version is the real me,}} and what makes us who we are?

options.label: Start with a definition
options.text: According to the dictionary, identity is who or what a person is. Identity is made up of many different factors, such as music, clothes, friends, family and language. All of these factors influence young people in different ways, both online and offline, and they can change over time.
options.textLong: According to the dictionary, identity is who or what a person is. Identity is made up of many different factors, such as music, clothes, friends, family and language. Some of these factors, such as family, are given to us, whereas others, such as hobbies, are a matter of choice. All of these factors influence young people in different ways, both online and offline, and they can change over time.
options.reject: A blog is not a dictionary: a definition is a weak hook, and nobody wants to read on. A blog post opens with something personal or surprising.
options.rejectDe: Ein Blog ist kein Wörterbuch: Eine Definition ist ein schwacher Einstieg, der niemanden neugierig macht.

options.label: Start with a scene
options.why: A short scene from everyday life shows the topic instead of explaining it.

map.music: {{Every Sunday night, I do my favourite thing:}} I build the perfect playlist for the week ahead. Each song has to fit my mood, from the Monday blues to Friday energy. {{Somewhere between track five and track six, I always start to wonder:}} what makes me … me?
map.languages: {{On Saturday mornings, I often}} help my grandpa in his garden, chatting away in broad Viennese dialect. An hour later, I’m usually online, joking in English with a gamer from Toronto. {{Same person, two completely different voices.}} So what makes me … me?

map.music: {{Every Sunday night, I do my favourite thing:}} I build the perfect playlist for the week ahead. Each song has to fit my mood, from the Monday blues to Friday energy. There’s a rap song for the bus, something calm for homework and a loud track for the walk home. {{Somewhere between track five and track six, I always start to wonder:}} what makes me … me?
map.languages: {{On Saturday mornings, I often}} help my grandpa in his garden, chatting away in broad Viennese dialect. {{Over lunch, my mum reminds me}} in perfect standard German that my homework is still waiting. An hour later, I’m usually online, joking in English with a gamer from Toronto. {{Same person, three completely different voices.}} So what makes me … me?

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction with two details about our blogger that lead to the big question.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit zwei Details über unsere Bloggerin oder unseren Blogger fertigschreiben, die zur großen Frage führen.

steps.q: Content point 1: what shapes young people’s identity?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: Was prägt die Identität junger Menschen? Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add examples of what shapes our blogger and other young people. Invent them, and don’t use the examples from the board.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann erfundene Beispiele ergänzen, was unsere Bloggerin oder unseren Blogger und andere Jugendliche prägt, nicht die Beispiele vom Beamer.

options.label: Music, friends, family
options.text: Identity has many different parts. Music is important for young people. Otherwise, many teenagers listen to hip-hop or pop and make their own playlists. Friends are important too, especially my best friend {FRIEND}. On the contrary, clothes are also important for a lot of people our age. Family plays a role as well, and so do hobbies.
options.textLong: Identity has many different parts. Music is important for young people. Otherwise, many teenagers listen to hip-hop or pop and make their own playlists. Friends are important too, especially my best friend {FRIEND}. On the contrary, clothes are also important for a lot of people our age. Family plays a role as well, and so do hobbies. The place where we grow up shapes us as well. Some teenagers play football, and others prefer art or computer games. Many young people in Austria speak a dialect at home with their grandparents.
options.reject: The linking words are wrong: ‘Otherwise’ suggests an alternative that isn’t there and ‘On the contrary’ contradicts nothing, so the ideas are just listed.
options.rejectDe: Die Linking words passen nicht: Otherwise ohne Alternative und On the contrary ohne Widerspruch; die Ideen werden nur aufgezählt.

options.label: Friends and style
options.why: The topic sentence links back to the introduction, and a personal example makes the point real.

map.music: {{Music is only one piece of the puzzle, [[though]].}} Friends shape us just as much [[because]] we pick up their jokes, their slang and even their hobbies. {{[[For example,]] my best friend}} {FRIEND} got me into climbing, and now I spend most weekends at the climbing wall. {{Style matters too, [[since]]}} our clothes speak before we do.
map.languages: {{Language is only one piece of the puzzle, [[though]].}} Friends shape us just as much [[because]] we pick up their jokes, their slang and even their hobbies. {{[[For example,]] my best friend}} {FRIEND} got me into climbing, and now I spend most weekends at the climbing wall. {{Style matters too, [[since]]}} our clothes speak before we do.

map.music: {{Music is only one piece of the puzzle, [[though]].}} Friends shape us just as much [[because]] we pick up their jokes, their slang and even their hobbies. {{[[For example,]] my best friend}} {FRIEND} got me into climbing, and now I spend most weekends at the climbing wall. {{Style matters too, [[since]]}} our clothes speak before we do. My old skinny jeans have made way for wide trousers with chalk marks on them, and I’ve never felt more like myself. {{[[That’s why]] I believe}} we become a little like the people we spend our time with.
map.languages: {{Language is only one piece of the puzzle, [[though]].}} Friends shape us just as much [[because]] we pick up their jokes, their slang and even their hobbies. {{[[For example,]] my best friend}} {FRIEND} got me into climbing, and now I spend most weekends at the climbing wall. {{Style matters too, [[since]]}} our clothes speak before we do. My old skinny jeans have made way for wide trousers with chalk marks on them, and I’ve never felt more like myself. {{[[That’s why]] I believe}} we become a little like the people we spend our time with.

options.label: Choice and chance
options.why: ‘However’ shows a real contrast: what we choose and what we are born into.

map.music: {{Music is something we choose, and so are}} our clothes and hobbies. {{[[However,]] a lot of who we are}} isn’t our choice: the family we grow up in and the place we call home. {{[[For instance,]]}} Sunday lunch at my grandparents’ is a ritual I’d never give up, [[even though]] it means getting up before noon.
map.languages: {{We choose our clothes and hobbies, and to some extent}} even the way we speak. {{[[However,]] a lot of who we are}} isn’t our choice: the family we grow up in and the place we call home. {{[[For instance,]]}} Sunday lunch at my grandparents’ is a ritual I’d never give up, [[even though]] it means getting up before noon.

map.music: {{Music is something we choose, and so are}} our clothes and hobbies. {{Our teenage years are a time for trying things out:}} we dye our hair blue or join a band for three weeks [[because]] that’s how we find out what really suits us. {{[[However,]] a lot of who we are}} isn’t our choice: the family we grow up in and the place we call home. {{[[For instance,]]}} Sunday lunch at my grandparents’ is a ritual I’d never give up, [[even though]] it means getting up before noon.
map.languages: {{We choose our clothes and hobbies, and to some extent}} even the way we speak. {{Our teenage years are a time for trying things out:}} we dye our hair blue or join a band for three weeks [[because]] that’s how we find out what really suits us. {{[[However,]] a lot of who we are}} isn’t our choice: the family we grow up in and the place we call home. {{[[For instance,]]}} Sunday lunch at my grandparents’ is a ritual I’d never give up, [[even though]] it means getting up before noon.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add examples of what shapes our blogger and other young people and explain how they change us. Invent them, and don’t use the examples from the board.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann erfundene Beispiele ergänzen, was unsere Bloggerin oder unseren Blogger und andere Jugendliche prägt, und erklären, wie es uns verändert; nicht die Beispiele vom Beamer.

steps.q: Content point 2: how do we show who we are online and offline?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: online und offline im Vergleich. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then compare online and offline in your own words: give one example for each (invent them).
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann online und offline mit je einem erfundenen Beispiel vergleichen.

options.label: Two different stages
options.why: A clear comparison: ‘by contrast’ and ‘while’ show the difference between the two worlds.
options.text: {{This all plays out on two stages: online and offline.}} Online, we can plan every detail: we pick the best photo, add a filter and delete anything embarrassing. Offline, [[by contrast,]] there’s no edit button. {{[[While]] my profile is full of}} concerts and sunsets, my classmates know someone who’s grumpy before ten and laughs far too loudly.
options.textLong: {{This all plays out on two stages: online and offline.}} Online, we can plan every detail: we pick the best photo, add a filter and delete anything embarrassing. Offline, [[by contrast,]] there’s no edit button. {{[[While]] my profile is full of}} concerts and sunsets, my classmates know someone who’s grumpy before ten and laughs far too loudly. {{The problem starts when}} likes decide what we post: some people delete a photo if it doesn’t get enough likes. Little by little, their profile shows what they think others want to see [[rather than]] who they really are.

options.label: My two lives
options.text: Online and offline, we show us in very different ways. For two years now, I’ve posted a photo every day, usually of concerts, sunsets or my breakfast, and everyone means my life is perfect. In the school, though, I’m much quieter than on my profile, and hardly anyone in my class knows about my secret account.
options.textLong: Online and offline, we show us in very different ways. For two years now, I’ve posted a photo every day, usually of concerts, sunsets or my breakfast, and everyone means my life is perfect. In the school, though, I’m much quieter than on my profile, and hardly anyone in my class knows about my secret account. Online, I choose every photo carefully and use filters, but offline nobody can edit what I say or do. My friends say the quiet me is much funnier. Sometimes I wonder which of my two lives is the real one.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘we show us’ (→ we show ourselves), ‘everyone means’ (→ everyone thinks) and ‘in the school’ (→ at school).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: we show us → ourselves, everyone means → everyone thinks („meinen“ heißt hier think), in the school → at school.

options.label: Not as fake as you think
options.why: Starts with a common opinion and then argues against it: a lively way to compare.
options.text: {{What about our online selves? Many adults think they are fake.}} I disagree. Online, we can show sides we hide in class, [[such as]] a love of poetry or our latest dance routine. {{[[On the other hand,]] it’s true that}} every post is carefully chosen, {{[[so]] a profile is more like}} a highlight reel than a diary.
options.textLong: {{What about our online selves? Many adults think they are fake.}} I disagree. Online, we can show sides we hide in class, [[such as]] a love of poetry or our latest dance routine. {{[[On the other hand,]] it’s true that}} every post is carefully chosen, {{[[so]] a profile is more like}} a highlight reel than a diary. {{Look at the accounts you follow:}} the posts we remember are rarely the perfect ones, but the ones that show a real hobby or a joke only that person would make. That’s not fake; it’s a part of us we choose to share.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then compare online and offline in your own words: give one example for each (invent them) and say what can go wrong online.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann online und offline mit je einem erfundenen Beispiel vergleichen und sagen, was online schiefgehen kann.

steps.q: Content point 3: what advice do we give readers who feel they have to fit in?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Tipps für Leser:innen, die sich unter Druck fühlen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add your own tips and a reason for each one.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Tipps mit Begründung ergänzen.

options.label: Three clear tips
options.why: ‘First of all’, ‘secondly’ and ‘thirdly’ give the tips a clear order.
options.text: {{But what if you feel you must fit in, online or offline?}} {{[[First of all,]] remember that}} almost everyone feels this way, even the most confident-looking people. {{[[Secondly,]] spend time with people who}} like you for who you are, not for what you wear. {{[[Thirdly,]]}} don’t compare your everyday life with other people’s best moments online.
options.textLong: {{But what if you feel you must fit in, online or offline?}} {{[[First of all,]] remember that}} almost everyone feels this way, even the most confident-looking people. Talk to a friend or a teacher you trust, and you’ll probably discover that they’ve felt exactly the same. {{[[Secondly,]] spend time with people who}} like you for who you are, not for what you wear. A team or a club is a good place to start. {{[[Thirdly,]]}} don’t compare your everyday life with other people’s best moments online [[because]] nobody posts their boring Tuesdays.

options.label: Fitting in or belonging?
options.why: One strong idea, explained with a contrast and backed up with examples.
options.text: {{Tired of trying to fit in, online or offline? Here’s my advice:}} look for a place where you can belong [[instead]]. Fitting in means changing yourself to be accepted, [[whereas]] belonging means being accepted as you are. {{You might find your people in}} a drama club, a choir or an online group for your unusual hobby.
options.textLong: {{Tired of trying to fit in, online or offline? Here’s my advice:}} look for a place where you can belong [[instead]]. Fitting in means changing yourself to be accepted, [[whereas]] belonging means being accepted as you are. {{You might find your people in}} a drama club, a choir or an online group for your unusual hobby. {{Once you find them,}} you’ll notice that you no longer think about every word or every outfit, and that feeling is worth more than a hundred likes from people who only know your profile.

options.label: Straight to the advice
options.text: My advice to readers who feel under pressure to fit in is simple. Readers who feel under pressure to fit in should remember that they are not alone. They can talk to friends, try new hobbies and spend less time on social media. In the end, nobody needs to feel under pressure to fit in.
options.textLong: My advice to readers who feel under pressure to fit in is simple. Readers who feel under pressure to fit in should remember that they are not alone. They can talk to friends, try new hobbies and spend less time on social media. Joining a club with people who share their interests can help, and so can an evening without a phone. Writing a diary before bed is another good idea. True friends accept people as they are. In the end, nobody needs to feel under pressure to fit in.
options.reject: This copies the words of the task (‘readers who feel under pressure to fit in’) instead of using your own. Use your own words and a range of structures.
options.rejectDe: Die Formulierung der Aufgabe („feel under pressure to fit in“) wird immer wieder abgeschrieben. Eigene Worte verwenden!

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add your own tips, with a reason or an example for each one.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eigene Tipps mit je einer Begründung oder einem Beispiel ergänzen.

steps.q: How do we end our blog post?
steps.de: Der Schluss rundet den Blogbeitrag ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then sum up our blogger’s answer in one sentence of your own and finish with a call to comment.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Antwort unserer Bloggerin oder unseres Bloggers in einem eigenen Satz zusammenfassen und mit einem Aufruf zum Kommentieren enden.

options.label: Ask the readers
options.why: Sums up the blogger’s answer and hands the question over to the readers.

map.music: {{[[All in all,]] there’s no single answer.}} Online and offline, I’m a mix of my friends, my family and about three hundred songs, and I’m happy with that mix. {{Now it’s your turn: what makes you … you?}} Tell me in the comments, along with your favourite song!
map.languages: {{[[All in all,]] there’s no single answer.}} Online and offline, I’m a mix of my friends, my family and the different ways I speak, and I’m happy with that mix. {{Now it’s your turn: what makes you … you?}} Tell me in the comments, in any language you like!

map.music: {{[[All in all,]] there’s no single answer.}} Online and offline, I’m a mix of my friends, my family and about three hundred songs, and I’m happy with that mix. Some parts will change and others will stay, but I’ve stopped trying to be someone else just to fit in. {{Now it’s your turn: what makes you … you?}} Tell me in the comments, along with your favourite song!
map.languages: {{[[All in all,]] there’s no single answer.}} Online and offline, I’m a mix of my friends, my family and the different ways I speak, and I’m happy with that mix. Some parts will change and others will stay, but I’ve stopped trying to be someone else just to fit in. {{Now it’s your turn: what makes you … you?}} Tell me in the comments, in any language you like!

options.label: A challenge
options.why: A memorable comparison, then a fun challenge that gets readers commenting.

map.music: {{[[To sum up,]] identity is less like a photo and more like a playlist:}} others add some of the tracks, but we decide which ones we play loudest. {{So here’s my challenge for you:}} describe yourself in three songs and post them in the comments. I can’t wait to hear them!
map.languages: {{[[To sum up,]] identity is less like a photo and more like a conversation:}} online or offline, we choose our own words. {{So here’s my challenge for you:}} describe yourself in three words, in any language, and post them in the comments. I can’t wait to read them!

map.music: {{[[To sum up,]] identity is less like a photo and more like a playlist:}} others add some of the tracks, but we decide which ones we play loudest. Online or offline, nobody else should choose the ones we skip. {{So here’s my challenge for you:}} describe yourself in three songs and post them in the comments. I can’t wait to hear them!
map.languages: {{[[To sum up,]] identity is less like a photo and more like a conversation:}} online or offline, we choose our own words. Some come from friends and family, others we learn on our own, and nobody else should tell us which ones to use. {{So here’s my challenge for you:}} describe yourself in three words, in any language, and post them in the comments. I can’t wait to read them!

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then sum up our blogger’s answer in two sentences of your own and finish with a call to comment.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Antwort unserer Bloggerin oder unseres Bloggers in zwei eigenen Sätzen zusammenfassen und mit einem Aufruf zum Kommentieren enden.

steps.q: Now that the blog post is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Den Titel wählen wir zuletzt: Er soll neugierig machen und zum ganzen Text passen.
steps.own: Short and catchy: the title should make readers curious about our post.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und griffig: Der Titel soll neugierig auf unseren Beitrag machen.

options.label: A personal title
options.why: Picks up our blogger’s angle, so readers know at once what makes this post special.

map.music: Who am I? Ask my playlist
map.languages: Dialect, German, English: which one is me?

options.label: A hint at the online part
options.why: Short and catchy, and it suggests that there is more to us than what we post.

options.label: A question
options.why: A question with two sides makes readers think about their own answer.

checks.en: A title that makes readers curious, with user name, date and time under it
The introduction hooks the readers with a question or a scene
All three content points: what shapes identity, online vs offline, advice
Five paragraphs; each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence linked to what came before
Linking words that really fit: contrast, reason, result, examples
Friendly blog style: contractions, questions and ‘you’, but no slang overload
The ending invites readers to comment

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Blogbeitrag auf B1+/B2-Niveau mit drei Inhaltspunkten nach SRDP-Muster und trainiert dabei Linking words für persönliche Gedankengänge, Topic Sentences und den lockeren, aber klar gegliederten Blog-Ton.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, Beamer im Vollbild. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5–6 min pro Absatz.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: rechts oben das Datum, als Überschrift „Blog post“ (wie am Beamer). Darunter 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (der Titel kommt zuletzt), darunter Username · Datum, Uhrzeit. Fünf Absätze, jeder beginnt nach einer Leerzeile; am Rand stehen Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3 und Conclusion. Linking words grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: 7 Entscheidungen (Aufhänger, Einleitung, Body 1–3, Schluss, Titel). Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Blog-Merkmale, 7 Entscheidungen à ca. 2 min, Abschreiben ca. 25 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (100 min): dieselben 7 Entscheidungen, aber längere Absätze: vor jeder Abstimmung 2 min Lesezeit für die langen Karten, Abschreiben ca. 40 min, am Ende 10 min Linking words und Checkliste. Gerüst kurz (realistisch ca. 60 min): 3 min Aufgabe und Aufhänger, pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 3 min Titel und 5 min Checkliste. In einer 50-Minuten-Stunde Titel und Checkliste am Beginn der nächsten Stunde. Gerüst lang (100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen, pro Absatz 2 min Lesen und Abstimmen, eigenes Schreiben 7–8 min bei Einleitung und Schluss, 11–12 min bei Body 1–3, je 2 min Vergleich; am Ende 3 min Titel und 4 min Checkliste.
teacher.traps: Introduction B (TA): Wörterbuch-Definition („According to the dictionary …“) statt Hook, kein Blog-Einstieg. Body 1 A (CC): Otherwise (keine Alternative) und On the contrary (kein Widerspruch) ohne Sinn, die Ideen werden nur aufgezählt. Body 2 B (LSA): we show us, everyone means, in the school. Body 3 C (LSR): übernimmt immer wieder die Formulierung der Aufgabe („readers who feel under pressure to fit in“), statt eigene Worte zu verwenden. Die Fallen haben in beiden Längen denselben Fehler. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Sensibles Thema: Geschrieben wird über junge Menschen allgemein und über eine erfundene Person mit dem Usernamen teen_in_progress; niemand muss Persönliches preisgeben. Hinweis auf Schulpsychologie bzw. Rat auf Draht (Tel. 147) bereithalten; Body 3 A rät in der langen Fassung, mit einer Vertrauensperson zu reden: guter Anlass, diese Anlaufstellen zu nennen. Geschlechtsidentität ist nicht Thema dieses Blogs. Im Gerüst-Modus schreiben alle über die erfundene Bloggerin oder den erfundenen Blogger, nicht über sich selbst. Der Blogbeitrag hat in beiden Längen genau fünf Absätze. Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen; jede Karte ist derselbe Absatz, nur ausführlicher (Einleitung und Schluss ca. 60–70 Wörter, Body 1–3 ca. 90–100). Markiert sind Linking words für den persönlichen Gedankengang (Gründe, Beispiele, Gegensätze, Nachgedanken im Plauderton), also über and und but hinaus (because, since, so, although, however, for example …) und auch nachgestelltes though; when, if und „So“ am Anfang einer Frage oder eines Aufrufs bleiben unmarkiert. Für den Namen der besten Freundin oder des besten Freundes nur erfundene Namen, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus pro Absatz ein zusätzliches eigenes Beispiel. Hausübung: ein Kommentar (ca. 150 Wörter) unter dem fertigen Blogbeitrag oder eine zweite Fassung mit dem anderen Aufhänger.
